title: Artemis II
description: Live orbital trajectory simulator for NASA’s Artemis II lunar mission. Three-body RK4 integration (Earth + Moon + Sun) calibrated against NASA mission control data — lunar flyby within 3 minutes of published time. Aviation-style scrolling tape gauges, real-time telemetry, time dilation tracking, and model fidelity indicators.

title: Optics Lab
description: Every optics diagram in the textbook is frozen at one angle — what happens when you drag it? An interactive browser-based simulator for exploring Snell’s law, total internal reflection, thin lens imaging, and chromatic dispersion with real-time ray tracing. Features wavelength-dependent Cauchy dispersion, spectral beam color rendering, and continuous parameter exploration through qualitative transitions like the critical angle and focal-point singularity. Built for physics students who want to see what the textbook can’t show.

title: 2D Particle Collision Lab
description: Interactive 2D oblique particle collision simulator. Explore elastic and inelastic collisions with adjustable masses, velocities, impact angles, and coefficient of restitution. Real-time animation with energy bars, momentum verification, and parametric sweeps. Why should I care? Because watching e = 0.5 is worth more than calculating it.

title: Degree Navigator
description: Interactive degree planning and curriculum design tool for UCO School of Engineering. Visual 8-semester grid with prerequisite tracking, critical path analysis, drag-and-drop course rearrangement, and what-if major change analysis across 7 engineering programs (EP, ME, EE, CE, BME).

title: Navier-Stokes Smoke Simulator
description: Real-time 2D smoke and fire simulator using Navier-Stokes equations computed entirely on the GPU via WebGL2 fragment shaders. Features interactive obstacle placement, wind tunnel mode, MacCormack advection, vorticity confinement, and experimental weather physics with atmospheric convection and precipitation.

title: Data Center Cooling Testbed
description: How much cooling does a 600-watt chip actually need — and what happens when the flow drops? An interactive thermal simulation of a modular bench-scale data center cooling system for ENGR 3211 Thermal Engineering Lab. Features ε-NTU heat exchanger modeling with two exchangers (shell-coil and plate stack), aluminum vs copper chip simulator material selection, counter-flow and co-current flow arrangement toggle, animated flow visualization with temperature color gradients, real-time transient response with 6-channel temperature traces, and a full energy balance dashboard (R_θ, UA, LMTD, ε, NTU).
imageAlt: Data Center Cooling Testbed - Interactive Thermal Simulation

title: The Work-Energy Principle
description: Two of the three terms in any energy problem reduce to numbers you can measure — the third falls out by subtraction. A unified treatment of the work-energy principle across mechanics and electrostatics, developing the energy equation as an accounting tool where conservative work (gravity, electric potential) collapses to scalar endpoint differences, kinetic energy reduces to two speed measurements, and nonconservative work — however complex — is determined by the residual. Parallel examples show how friction on an inclined plane maps directly onto resistive forces on a charged particle, and how Stoke’s drag and Drude-model conduction share identical mathematical structure.

title: Capacitor Dielectric Lab
description: Dielectrics change everything about a capacitor — but you can’t see why until you twist the knobs yourself. An interactive RC circuit simulator for exploring parallel-plate capacitors with 9 interchangeable dielectric materials. Features real-time charging/discharging waveforms on a phosphor-style oscilloscope, τ markers, Kirchhoff’s Voltage Law verification, energy storage tracking, and a retro-futuristic cockpit interface. Supports both free exploration and guided laboratory modes for the PSE-II course.
imageAlt: Capacitor Dielectric Lab - Interactive RC Circuit Simulator

title: ECDO Watch
description: Is the Earth quietly shifting on its axis — and can we see it in the data? An interactive 3D globe and geophysical monitoring dashboard tracking real-time Kp/Dst geomagnetic indices, Earth orientation parameters (polar motion, length of day), C20 gravity coefficients, deep seismicity, and volcanic activity with animated radial pulses. Features an ancient monument alignment workbench analyzing 97 structures against a hypothesized former pole (Np’), with measured bearing axes, projected great-circle lines, signal quality heatmap overlay, and cross-channel coherence analysis across multiple time windows.
imageAlt: ECDO Watch - 3D Globe and Geophysical Dashboard

title: Thermofluidic Finance
description: What if your bank account obeyed the same laws as a tank of pressurized fluid? A mathematical framework in which personal finance operates as a dynamical system governed by fluid mechanics and thermodynamics. Cash accounts behave as interconnected reservoirs of incompressible fluid. Volatile investments behave as compressible media subject to an exact First Law: unrealized gains are heat absorbed, realized gains are work extracted.

title: On Dynamical Systems
description: Springs, circuits, and populations all obey the same equation — here is the proof. A unifying mathematical framework for dynamical systems built on the product structure Behavior = Response × Drive. Parts I–IX develop the primordial pattern, potential energy and the three energy modes (potential, kinetic, dissipative), impedance and bond-graph power conjugacy, the complete cross-domain analogy, conservation laws and constitutive relations, spectral geometry of the state manifold, and a causal underdetermination theorem showing that behavior alone cannot resolve intrinsic response from extrinsic drive without auxiliary assumptions.

title: Electrostatics Lab
description: Electric fields are invisible — this tool lets you reach in and explore them. An interactive 3D web-based visualization supporting 11 charge configurations (point charges, dipoles, extended objects, and plate geometries). Features real-time RK4 field line integration with advanced spherical coordinate seeding, vector field glyphs, 3D equipotential surfaces via marching cubes, 2D slice views with heat maps, and a camera-aligned live cross-section. Multiple visualization modes enable students to develop spatial intuition about electromagnetic phenomena through interactive exploration.

title: SPECTRUM Market Analytics
description: Markets produce thousands of signals daily — which ones actually matter? A multi-dimensional market intelligence dashboard providing comprehensive asset analysis across stocks and cryptocurrencies. Features radar charts for fundamental, technical, and sentiment analysis, price history with moving averages, sector comparisons, ESG profiling, and macro factor visualization. Presents complex market signals through an intuitive dark-themed interface with tabbed navigation across analysis dimensions.

title: Eisenhower Task Manager
description: Not all tasks are created equal, and most to-do lists pretend otherwise. A tactical task prioritization instrument styled as an electronic warfare control station — four CRT monitors with phosphor-tinted screens, anti-glare hoods, and scanline overlays display the Eisenhower Matrix quadrants. Features five views (Matrix, List, Gantt, Analytics, Calendar), completion verification with LED ratings, planning/execution scoring, and recurring task support. Server-based single source of truth accessible via Tailscale.

title: Dynamical Systems Lab
description: Chaos, bifurcations, and strange attractors are easier to understand when you can twist the knobs yourself. An interactive React-based laboratory for exploring and visualizing dynamical systems. Includes implementations of classical systems like Lorenz attractors, pendulums, oscillators, and bifurcation phenomena. Provides real-time 3D visualization and parameter adjustment for understanding complex system behavior.

title: Two-Body Gravitational Free Fall
description: When two masses fall toward each other under gravity, the textbook shortcut gets the answer wrong. A comprehensive analysis deriving final velocities and collision times using conservation of energy, work-energy principles, and classical mechanics. Includes comparison with kinematic approximations and demonstrates the importance of accounting for variable acceleration in gravitational systems.

title: Problem-Solving and Critical Path Reasoning
description: Most frameworks tell you what to think — this one tells you what to question. A systematic approach to problem-solving that guides practitioners through four stages: Observation (known knowns), Analysis (known unknowns), Inference (unknown knowns), and Exploration (unknown unknowns). The PSCPR Guide Sheet provides a structured method to test claims against nulls using facts, patterns, and stories to reach evidence-based conclusions.
imageAlt: Problem-Solving and Critical Path Reasoning Thumbnail

title: Inferential Dynamics
description: What if logical fallacies and mechanical instabilities are the same phenomenon? This work develops a synthesis between classical logic and dynamical systems theory. The canonical inference square – Modus Ponens (MP), Modus Tollens (MT), Affirming the Consequent (AC), and Denying the Antecedent (DA) – admits a natural interpretation as a stability matrix. Valid inferences (MP, MT) act as negative-feedback eigendirections, damping error and converging toward a stable attractor: truth. Fallacies (AC, DA) operate as positive-feedback eigendirections, amplifying error and driving divergence. The symmetry parallels James Clerk Maxwell’s On Governors (1868), where Aristotle’s concern with valid inference, Maxwell’s concern with mechanical stability, and the modern eigenvalue criterion are recognized as structurally isomorphic descriptions of reality.

title: Dynamic Control of an Aeropendulum
description: A propeller-driven pendulum testbed for investigating what control theories survive contact with reality. Implements four control modes — manual, static PID angle hold, amplitude-regulated oscillation, and active damping — on custom hardware with dual-sensor fusion (AS5600 magnetic encoder + MPU6050 IMU). Features circular-mean tare calibration, wrap-safe EMA filtering, anti-windup integral clamp, PWM slew rate limiting, and a custom 3D-printed enclosure through 18+ CAD iterations.

title: Rebound Pendulum
description: A ball bounces back — but how much energy did it surrender? The rebound pendulum connects rebound height, velocity, and angular deflection to the coefficient of restitution, revealing how a simple device can yield deep insights into material response and collision efficiency. It bridges theory and measurement, offering experimental methods for quantifying energy loss in a system traditionally used to model ideal motion.

title: Certainty, Inference, and Comprehension
description: Critical thinking is a term widely used in academics yet is a weak form of logical inference akin to abduction, and especially weak as compared to induction or a stronger form of inference – deduction. By establishing a framework which prioritizes questions over answers and function over form, and by investigating modes of inferential logic, reexamining the scientific method, and distinguishing between comprehension and understanding, a deductive "critical path" of logical inference is prescribed to effectively prosecute hypotheses and disrupt paradigm.

title: Horizontal Frame Centering Algorithm
description: Hanging pictures evenly on a wall shouldn’t require guesswork — and it doesn’t. Derives equations to determine optimal frame placement such that gaps between frame edges and wall edges are uniform, with analytical formulas for calculating frame center positions given wall width, frame width, and frame count.

title: Universe of Proportions
description: From Kepler’s orbits to DNA, the deepest insights in science reduce to one operation: division. A conceptual exploration of ratios and proportions as the universal language underlying physics, engineering, biology, chemistry, and mathematics. From Babylonian clay tablets to modern physics, the work demonstrates how analogical thinking through proportions reveals deep structural patterns. Explores applications from Kepler’s laws to genetic ratios, spring constants to photosynthesis, Archimedes’ principle to the golden ratio.

title: Fundamental Principles - On Analogies (continued)
description: If a spring and a capacitor obey the same equation, are they really different systems? Extends the source-field-force model across diverse domains, exploring how fundamental mathematical structures reveal isomorphic patterns in mechanics, electromagnetism, thermodynamics, and abstract systems, demonstrating the power of analogical reasoning in physics and philosophy.

title: On Physical Analogies
description: Gravity, electrostatics, and heat flow look different — until you write them in the same language. A foundational exploration of structural analogies between physical systems, introducing the unifying concept of sources interacting with fields to produce forces. Examines how this framework applies across mechanics, electrostatics, and thermodynamics, revealing deep connections between seemingly distinct phenomena.

title: Gravitational Radiation
description: What if gravitational fields gain energy instead of radiating it away? A Masters thesis extending Oliver Heaviside’s 1893 analogy between gravitation and electromagnetism. By deriving gravitational field equations, retarded potentials, and radiation patterns using Maxwell-Heaviside formalism, this work models how accelerated masses emit gravitational radiation analogously to electric dipole radiation. Notably, the formulation predicts a reversal in the Poynting vector — a paradox that challenges our understanding of gravitational energy flow and the speed of gravitational propagation.

title: Disk Cam Synthesis
description: Custom cam profiles normally require expensive commercial software — this tool goes from motion spec to 3D-printer G-code for free. Users input desired motion profiles and the system calculates the required cam geometry, kinematic derivatives (position, velocity, acceleration, jerk), animated simulations, and exportable CAD files. Designed as an affordable, educational alternative, it bridges theory, simulation, and physical manufacturing.

title: Nonlinear Human Population Growth Modeling
description: Every population model fits the past perfectly — but their futures disagree by billions. A collaborative research project deriving nonlinear growth models from chemical kinetics theory and fitting them to nearly 2,000 years of historical data. Using Excel’s Solver to optimize parameters, we compared multiple model forms (exponential, logistic, power-law) across different data windows. Results demonstrate that while models agree on historical data, their long-term forecasts diverge dramatically — some predicting exponential growth, others stabilization or collapse.

title: Gravitational Wave Detector
description: Can a Zener diode detect gravitational waves? We built the apparatus to find out. This senior design project constructed and tested a low-cost tabletop detector based on R.T. Cahill’s theoretical framework for quantum fluctuations in reverse-biased Zener diodes. The apparatus was systematically tested for sensitivity to temperature, microwaves, humidity, and vibrations. While no conclusive evidence of gravitational wave detection was found, the work provides design specifications and test procedures for continued investigation into quantum detector sensitivity.
